title: 'Acute confusion' with hyponatremia: possible metabolic encephalopathy
discharge_summary: SYNTHETIC CASE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Synthetic Patient 10, 79-year-old male. MRN: SYN-0010
Reason for admission: Acute confusion and fever.

His daughter reports he has mild dementia but normally recognizes family, feeds himself, and walks with a cane. On arrival he was disoriented to time and place, could not follow two-step commands, and had fluctuating attention. He required a sitter for safety on days 1-3.
Sodium was 126 mmol/L. Urinalysis showed pyuria, and urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae. CT of the head showed no acute findings. Ammonia and TSH were normal.

He was treated with IV ceftriaxone and fluid restriction, and sodium was checked every 6 hours, rising to 134 by day 4. Mental status returned to his baseline on day 4, and he was oriented to person and place at discharge.
1. Urinary tract infection due to Klebsiella pneumoniae
Discharge plan: Oral cefuroxime to complete 7 days. Fluid restriction 1.5 L per day. Repeat sodium in 3 days.

expected.notes: 'Acute confusion' is a symptom. Acute change from baseline, inattention, sitter, and correction of sodium with return to baseline point to metabolic encephalopathy (G93.41, MCC) or delirium due to a known physiological condition (F05). Query; the case already has a CC (E87.1), so this would raise it to MCC. Toxic or toxic metabolic encephalopathy (G92.8/G92.9, MCC) is also accepted: the code is only used for the CC/MCC lookup, and the provider chooses the diagnosis.
